questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed in the syllabus coverage for “Integrating Third-Party Services”?
questions.explanation: The attached FastAPI syllabus lists “Email service integration” under this lesson. The remaining syllabus subtopics are preserved in the lesson file for complete coverage.

questions.prompt: According to the worked example in “Integrating Third-Party Services”, which result should the learner verify?
options: Without Authorization: Bearer <token>, the request is rejected. This demo does not authenticate or authorize the token.
The app publishes itself to production and passes all tests automatically.
HTTP 500 is returned for every valid request.
Input validation and authorization are disabled by design.
questions.answer_key: Without Authorization: Bearer <token>, the request is rejected. This demo does not authenticate or authorize the token.
questions.explanation: The worked example explicitly documents this expected result. Reproduce it locally in the listed environment before treating it as tested behavior.

questions.prompt: Which integration practice best matches this topic? (Integrating Third-Party Services)
options: Bound uploads or requests, set timeouts, validate untrusted data and handle failures explicitly
Assume all external services always succeed
Retry every request forever without checking idempotency
Store uploaded files under raw client-supplied paths
questions.answer_key: Bound uploads or requests, set timeouts, validate untrusted data and handle failures explicitly
questions.explanation: External inputs and services can fail or be hostile; bound resources, validate requests and make retries safe.
